newsitem.title: CANADA: Philippines miller shopping for high protein wheat.
newsitem.headline: Philippines miller shopping for high protein wheat.

text.p: One of the Philippines largest flour millers said on Tuesday it is seeking high protein bread and noodle wheats because recent imports fell below its quality specifications.

"Lately, we've had problems with U.S. soft wheat because they've had low protein in the 1996 production. At present we're seeing about 9.7 percent protein," General Milling Corporation's quality control manager Artemio Vasquez said.
Philippino millers seek 14 percent protein content in Canadian and U.S. hard red spring wheats and 10 to 11 percent in soft white wheats for consistency in milling, Vasquez said.
"We prefer the CWRS (Canada Western Red Spring wheat) at 14 percent," said Vasquez, who was in Winnipeg for a wheat quality seminar.
"We get our wheat from the U.S. and Canada, not from Australia," he noted.
About 60 percent of bakeries in the Philippines are not mechanized and rely on uniform baking characteristics in the flour they buy, he said.
The Philippines' millers sourced up to 90 percent of their wheat import needs from Canada in 1992 but levels since fell to about 40 percent due to reduced Canadian output, he said.
"We'll decide (whether to source more from Canada) once we receive that first shipment from Canada in July. After that, hopefully we won't have any problems with that soft wheat," he said.
